Paradise Lost - Bazaruto Island View Estate

By: Graham Coetzer | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
Crystal clear waters and white sandy beaches, investors were thrilled at the prospect of purchasing property in Mozambique - now they say they've been duped by a South African businessman.

Unique Selling Point:
Crystal clear waters, white sand and friendly locals – this is the promise sold to willing buyers by Ettienne Erasmus, a prolific businessman who has been selling property opportunities in Mozambique to South Africans since at least 2008. The problem is, after he takes your money, the promised property does not seem to materialise.
His sales pitch is that South Africa is a ‘sinking ship’ with a failing economy, whereas Mozambique offers safety, friendly locals keen for investments, and a growing economy.

Summary:
In 2008, Erasmus established Bazaruto Island View Estate (he is again the sole director) and began to sell property investment opportunities, initially claiming that clients would have full title ownership of the properties, then that they had 99 year leases, and finally demanding that clients pay extra and build on the stands within 5 years. He advertised extensively on Radio Pretoria and Facebook.
It seems a number of people invested in BIVE, which was represented as a luxury “security lifestyle estate” in the making, with promises of a medical centre, resort, marina, etc. People invested either to own a holiday home or to build and sell at a profit.

In 2016, a string of articles appeared in the Lowvelder, with alleged victims claiming to have invested tens or hundreds of thousands, only to see no return years later. Erasmus admitted that he had started selling plots in 2009 despite receiving permission only in 2012. He claimed perceptions of conflict in the area were slowing development and construction had only started on two houses. He also claimed that 70% of the stands had been sold. Investors claimed they had been charged levies despite no electricity or water connection; the contractor told Lowvelder he had withdrawn because nothing was happening.
One Lowvelder article revealed that the images featured on BIVE’s website with its logo were actually taken from the sites of luxury resorts around the world. Similarly, the pictures on BIVE’s website gallery appear to be of a nearby resort called Casa de Lua, as well as a fishing charter company called Big Blue Vilankulo.

From about 2014 onwards, Erasmus and his partner Grace Bagnari (Schutte) abandoned the BIVE social media pages and started posting on a variety of other groups and pages, including Mozambique Properties (MozProp), Destination Mozambique, Opportunities in Mozambique, Vilanculos Beach Properties and MozForum. They seem to have been avoiding the BIVE name, but the sales pitch is the same.

Further information:
We received images of the site as of yesterday and there has been no further development than the last images placed on facebook by erasmus in 2014
He claimed to have sold 80 properties, which at the very least would have given him about R40 million, but possibly in excess of R80 mil
We will be going to see Etienne with hidden camera as "investors" to get the pitch
Our case studies still have all their documentation, emails etc
One case study has provided us with a whatsappl in which Erasmus threatens him and his wife - very obnoxious and crude language etc etc
I have an attorney, Coenraad Kukuk, who represented a case study in the pta high court against Erasmus, who knows property laws in mozambique, who will do an interview
All the case studies were also charged levies, as Erasmus continued to string them along with promises of completion happening soon.

Case studies - Karel Swart - Spent R1 350 000 of his pension money - also worked for Erasmus - contract said he could take occupation in 2010
Awie Human - Lost R300 000 to Erasmus
Snyman Cronje - Lost R600 000. His brother also bought stands and lost R600 000 as well. Brother, who lives in America and earns US dollars, actually continued to pay levies for years.

PLEASE NOTE - case studies for this story are not very diverse, Erasmus targets mainly white afrikaners who are worried about crime etc in SA.

Script:


Paradise Lost
First Draft Script
9 July 2020

Voice
This is Vilanculos in Mozambique, situated about 700km from the country’s capital Maputo. When South African businessman Ettienne Erasmus announced he was developing the luxury Bazaruto Island View Estate there in 2008, many South Africans jumped at the chance to own their own slice of paradise.

Link Mac
Imagine crystal clear water, pristine beaches, and an endless ocean view. That’s the dream that investors were sold.

Voice
Erasmus and his business partner Grace Bagnari have promoted the Bazaruto Island View Estate, also known as BIVE, on radio, television and via social media platforms where they post videos like these.

Sound Up BIVE Marketing Video
Investors with an eye for opportunity are signalled to get in while the tide is coming in, and take advantage before prices escalate.

Voice
But investors say that while Erasmus company Vilankulos Beach Properties raked in millions since 2008, these two unfinished houses, a borehole, this beach bar and this fence make up the bulk of what’s been built at BIVE today. Snyman Cronje says he visited the site in Vilanculos in 2008.

Sound Up Snyman
While we were there we actually signed for the stands.

Voice
Cronje agreed to pay R365 000 for two stands at the development. Karel and Memory Swart also bought a stand at BIVE that year.

Sound Up Karel
That stand cost me R255 000.

Voice
This man, who we’ll call Mr X as he’s asked us to hide his identity, says Erasmus promised lucrative returns for early investors, and in 2009 he purchased multiple stands at BIVE.

Sound Up Mr X
Because its an investment, you can later sell off some of your stands and take that money and build your house on the estate.

Voice
Phase 1 of BIVE was supposed to be a secure residential estate.

Sound Up Snyman Cronje
Mac: You saw the paperwork, you saw everything, and to you this looked legit?

Snyman: The first thing they said they are going to develop is the guard house… there was supposed to be a boat launch where you can take your boat there.

Voice
In fact the full list of amenities offered in 2009 included:
- a secure gate house
a Lodge / Restaurant
a Beach Bar
a Dive Centre
and a Convenience store.

Sound Up Snyman
Everything that’s in place for a nice development.

Voice
Over the next two years investors say Erasmus promised even bigger things for the future of the BIVE project.

Sound Up Mr X
Mr X: He’s busy with developments on hospitals, restaurants, hotels, boat clubs, yacht clubs. It was just a fantastic picture.

Voice
But by 2012 our case studies had grown disillusioned with the project since there was still no:
Secure gate house
Lodge / Restaurant
Dive centre
or Convenience store.

Erasmus had told them he’d spent millions developing the estate, but they felt they’d bought a white elephant.

Sound Up Snyman
I mean you need a development, if there’s a development then I can build.

Link Mac
So with the exception of two half built houses and a couple of dirt roads, there really isn’t much here. So the question is where is all of that money?

Voice
To find out we sent our producer in to pose as a prospective buyer. In this voice recording both Ettiene and Grace are still promising to build their gatehouse, 12 years later.

Sound Up Voice Recording
Producer: And it would have guards, the whole works?

Ettiene: Absolutely, no you’ll have a proper… We’ll have an entrance gate at the top here, and then you’ll have a proper security setup complex there.

Grace: The gate house

Ettiene: Ja the gate house.

Producer: I saw you had like a mock up of what it would look like hey?

Ettiene and Grace: Yes

Producer: And thats the idea?

Ettiene and Grace: Yes

Voice
After the meeting we asked them for an interview, and they agreed meet us at a restaurant in Johannesburg. Erasmus says they’ve sold 86 stands on the first phase of the estate.

Sound Up Ettiene
Mac: How much money was raised?

Ettiene: It’s roughly about between sixteen and eighteen million.

Mac: how much of that was spent on the development?

Ettiene: Absolutely everything.

Mac: Ok and what were some of the thing that were then developed there?

Ettiene: Well obviously all your, the streets, and the authorisations, and the up keep of the rights, and obviously the marketing campaigns was some of the most expensive over a longer period of time.

Voice
Which means that investors who still want to build homes on their stands are stuck with what’s on site currently. To add insult to injury, they say they were contractually bound to pay levies.

Sound Up Mr X
we said why must we pay levy there is nothing… No development, so why must we pay levy, no facilities, so what’s the levy for?

Sound Up Ettiene
When they signed the contract it stipulated they must pay levies, that’s obviously to maintain the infrastructure that’s there, you have to pay the land taxes, we make fire breaks every year and we’ve got people permanently on the property. But again you sign an agreement, you sign an agreement and then you have to keep to the agreement. Because if you expect me to keep to it, they must also keep to it.

Voice
Despite the problems, some investors did actually start building their houses. This is the partially completed unit 10 on the BIVE estate, which was supposed to belong to Martin and Sophia Haupt. The original building contract was signed in 2013. But because of a family tragedy they’ve declined to be interviewed for this insert, but have given Carte Blanche their blessing to tell their story. They took Erasmus to court in 2015 to prevent him from selling the unit, but later abandoned the case because of cross border jurisdiction. According to their affidavit they paid Erasmus a total of R5,5 million to build their dream holiday home. At the time quantity surveyor Eddie Moll inspected the site on their behalf.

Sound Up Eddie
Eddie: They flew me up and we spent four days there and I was actually quite shocked to see what was actually built on site, compared to the actual payments and the value of the property claimed to have been constructed on that site.

Voice
According to Moll’s findings the total value of the construction to unit 10 only amounted to R807 000.

Sound Up Eddie
And I was quite generous when I valued it at average market related rates compared to Vilanculos and that typical construction in that area.

Voice
In his opposing affidavit Erasmus disputed the amount of R5.5 million.

Sound Up Ettiene
Mac: Now in your opposing affidavit you did admit that you received a total of R4 783 196 from the Haupts, right?

Ettiene: Ja,

Mac: Is that true?

Ettiene: if that’s in my documents then that’s right.

Voice
He questions a South African quantity surveyor’s ability to value projects in Mozambique and blames the fall out with the Haupts on them making too many design changes to their home.

Sound Up Ettiene
We were totally lenient with them, in an unrealistic manner. And so many things happened during that two years. A house thats supposed to be built in four to six months, in the end took two years.

Sound Up Eddie
I tried to set up a little round table with him, we could not get to any basic principals to be agreed upon, on values of the structure, on where’s the money, where’s the building.

Voice
Erasmus says he did have the funding to develop the whole BIVE resort he promised.

Sound Up Ettiene
And what I have here was the funding being approved.

Voice
But he claims his funders were scared away by bad publicity of the BIVE estate, all of which he blames on one man.

Sound Up Ettiene
We were interrupted by a very unfortunate thing, which was Mr Carlos Carvalho.

Voice
Erasmus says Carvalho scared away his funders by questioning the legality of the BIVE project in Mozambique on social media and assisting the Lowvelder newspaper in a series of expose’s they ran on BIVE in 2016.

Sound Up Erasmus
And then you get a person like this, which is very unusual, to actually blatantly go on the attack.

Voice
Carvalho declined to comment on the matter. Either way, our case studies say they’d lost all hope in the development years before the first article was published.

Sound Up Mr X
Mac: When did you decide that’s it, I’m done, I’m walking away from this?

Mr X: About 2012, 2013 I said well rather forget about it…

Mac: Right it off?

Mr X: Right it off.

Sound Up Ettiene
Mac: I’m saying since 2008 this is the promise and the marketing material…

Ettiene: We didn’t change, it will be there.

Mac: Nothing has changed, but nothing of it has happened?

Ettiene: Not yet, not yet.

Voice
Despite having very little to show for BIVE after 12 years of development, Erasmus doesn’t like the media questioning his project, and see’s it as a threat to his investors - despite the fact that they’d approached us.

Sound Up Mr X
And I said this is enough. And I then had a discussion with other investors and I then forwarded it to Carte Blanche.

Sound Up Ettiene
Ettiene: And I see Carte Blanche as a threat to our development, and I see it a threat to them, and that is utter stupidity.

Mac: Let’s get it right, What I’m saying to you is that individuals made allegations against you.

Ettiene: Ja, exactly

Mac: What we are doing right now is giving you the right of reply to what these allegations are.

Ettiene: Ja i know, and I’m using it.

Mac: It’s not Carte Blanche, we didn’t look for you, we didn’t know you from a bar of soap. It’s
people that came to us, making these allegations against you.

Ettiene: Ja.

Voice:
And those same people don’t feel like they got their money’s worth.

Sound Up Snyman
Stay away, you’re going to lose all your money. If you really want, I’ll sell you mine, for half price.











Promo 1
Voice
We investigate how a well-known South African businessman’s promises of an exotic estate development in Mozambique cost investors millions, and why years later they have very little to show for it.

Promo 2
Voice
It seemed like the perfect investment - owning a holiday home in a luxury estate in Mozambique. But for investors who spent millions, their dream homes have turned into the ultimate nightmare.

Promo 3
Voice
Pristine beaches, crystal clear waters and a luxury estate, that’s the dream buyers were sold. But after investors spent millions, the developer hasn’t delivered on his side of the bargain.

Voice But he claims his funders were scared away by bad publicity of the BIVE estate, all of which he blames on one man. Sound Up Ettiene We were interrupted by a very unfortunate thing, which was Mr Carlos Carvalho. Voice Erasmus says Carvalho scared away his funders by questioning the legality of the BIVE project in Mozambique on social media and assisting the Lowvelder newspaper in a series of expose’s they ran on BIVE in 2016. Sound Up Erasmus And then you get a person like this, which is very unusual, to actually blatantly go on the attack. Voice Carvalho declined to comment on the matter. Either way, our case studies say they’d lost all hope in the development years before the first article was published. Sound Up Mr X Mac: When did you decide that’s it, I’m done, I’m walking away from this? Mr X: About 2012, 2013 I said well rather forget about it… Mac: Right it off? Mr X: Right it off. Sound Up Ettiene Mac: I’m saying since 2008 this is the promise and the marketing material… Ettiene: We didn’t change, it will be there. Mac: Nothing has changed, but nothing of it has happened? Ettiene: Not yet, not yet. Voice Despite having very little to show for BIVE after 12 years of development, Erasmus doesn’t like the media questioning his project, and see’s it as a threat to his investors - despite the fact that they’d approached us. Sound Up Mr X And I said this is enough. And I then had a discussion with other investors and I then forwarded it to Carte Blanche. Sound Up Ettiene Ettiene: And I see Carte Blanche as a threat to our development, and I see it a threat to them, and that is utter stupidity. Mac: Let’s get it right, What I’m saying to you is that individuals made allegations against you. Ettiene: Ja, exactly Mac: What we are doing right now is giving you the right of reply to what these allegations are. Ettiene: Ja i know, and I’m using it. Mac: It’s not Carte Blanche, we didn’t look for you, we didn’t know you from a bar of soap. It’s people that came to us, making these allegations against you. Ettiene: Ja. Voice: And those same people don’t feel like they got their money’s worth. Sound Up Snyman Stay away, you’re going to lose all your money. If you really want, I’ll sell you mine, for half price. Promo 2 Voice It seemed like the perfect investment - owning a holiday home in a luxury estate in Mozambique. But for investors who spent millions, their dream homes have turned into the ultimate nightmare. Promo 3 Voice Pristine beaches, crystal clear waters and a luxury estate, that’s the dream buyers were sold. But after investors spent millions, the developer hasn’t delivered on his side of the bargain.

metadata.One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...): Crystal clear waters and white sandy beaches, investors were thrilled at the prospect of purchasing property in Mozambique - now they say they've been duped by a South African businessman.
metadata.Unique Selling Point: Crystal clear waters, white sand and friendly locals – this is the promise sold to willing buyers by Ettienne Erasmus, a prolific businessman who has been selling property opportunities in Mozambique to South Africans since at least 2008. The problem is, after he takes your money, the promised property does not seem to materialise. His sales pitch is that South Africa is a ‘sinking ship’ with a failing economy, whereas Mozambique offers safety, friendly locals keen for investments, and a growing economy.
metadata.Summary: In 2008, Erasmus established Bazaruto Island View Estate (he is again the sole director) and began to sell property investment opportunities, initially claiming that clients would have full title ownership of the properties, then that they had 99 year leases, and finally demanding that clients pay extra and build on the stands within 5 years. He advertised extensively on Radio Pretoria and Facebook. It seems a number of people invested in BIVE, which was represented as a luxury “security lifestyle estate” in the making, with promises of a medical centre, resort, marina, etc. People invested either to own a holiday home or to build and sell at a profit. In 2016, a string of articles appeared in the Lowvelder, with alleged victims claiming to have invested tens or hundreds of thousands, only to see no return years later. Erasmus admitted that he had started selling plots in 2009 despite receiving permission only in 2012. He claimed perceptions of conflict in the area were slowing development and construction had only started on two houses. He also claimed that 70% of the stands had been sold. Investors claimed they had been charged levies despite no electricity or water connection; the contractor told Lowvelder he had withdrawn because nothing was happening. One Lowvelder article revealed that the images featured on BIVE’s website with its logo were actually taken from the sites of luxury resorts around the world. Similarly, the pictures on BIVE’s website gallery appear to be of a nearby resort called Casa de Lua, as well as a fishing charter company called Big Blue Vilankulo. From about 2014 onwards, Erasmus and his partner Grace Bagnari (Schutte) abandoned the BIVE social media pages and started posting on a variety of other groups and pages, including Mozambique Properties (MozProp), Destination Mozambique, Opportunities in Mozambique, Vilanculos Beach Properties and MozForum. They seem to have been avoiding the BIVE name, but the sales pitch is the same.
metadata.Further information: We received images of the site as of yesterday and there has been no further development than the last images placed on facebook by erasmus in 2014 He claimed to have sold 80 properties, which at the very least would have given him about R40 million, but possibly in excess of R80 mil We will be going to see Etienne with hidden camera as "investors" to get the pitch Our case studies still have all their documentation, emails etc One case study has provided us with a whatsappl in which Erasmus threatens him and his wife - very obnoxious and crude language etc etc I have an attorney, Coenraad Kukuk, who represented a case study in the pta high court against Erasmus, who knows property laws in mozambique, who will do an interview All the case studies were also charged levies, as Erasmus continued to string them along with promises of completion happening soon. Case studies - Karel Swart - Spent R1 350 000 of his pension money - also worked for Erasmus - contract said he could take occupation in 2010 Awie Human - Lost R300 000 to Erasmus Snyman Cronje - Lost R600 000. His brother also bought stands and lost R600 000 as well. Brother, who lives in America and earns US dollars, actually continued to pay levies for years. PLEASE NOTE - case studies for this story are not very diverse, Erasmus targets mainly white afrikaners who are worried about crime etc in SA.
